problem: Learned visual navigation policies are frozen after training, so they generalize poorly to unseen scenes. For example, they repeat the same collision or get-stuck mistake many times, because no reward or supervision is available at test time to adapt with.
motivation: Humans keep learning while they perform a task and adapt to new environments through interaction, without explicit supervision. Navigation offers plenty of self-supervised interaction signal, such as collisions and revisits. A gradient-based meta-learner such as MAML could adapt to a new scene with a few SGD steps, provided the adaptation loss needs no reward.
key_idea: Meta-train an A3C navigation policy together with a learned self-supervised interaction loss (a small temporal-conv network over recent LSTM states and policies). Gradient steps on this loss, taken every k steps within an episode and also at test time, are optimized (MAML-style) to improve the supervised navigation loss.
insight:
A first-order Taylor expansion shows the objective trains the interaction-loss gradient to align with the navigation-loss gradient. This lets the agent keep 'training' at inference without rewards. It also explains why a learned loss beats hand-crafted ones:
- Learned SAVN reaches 40.86 SR / 16.15 SPL, versus 39.52 / 15.12 (diversity) and 38.06 / 14.36 (prediction).
- The hand-crafted losses raise success but not efficiency.

The ablations show the gain is not just from extra losses or memory:
- A3C with the prediction loss as an auxiliary gets 34.80 SR, versus 38.06 when the same loss is used for inner-loop adaptation.
- A3C with self-attention memory over the last 6 LSTM states gets 34.30 SR, versus 40.86 for SAVN.
- More interaction-gradient steps monotonically raise SR (figure only).
- SAVN's failed-action ratio drops as the episode progresses, i.e., it learns from collisions within the episode.
method: Base policy: an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet18 feature map is fused with the GloVe embedding of the target class. A pointwise conv follows, then an LSTM, then a linear layer producing policy π_θ and value v_θ. Trained with an actor-critic navigation loss L_nav (reward +5 for finding the target, -0.01 per step).

Self-supervised adaptation (inner loop): every k=6 steps, one SGD step (α=1e-4) is taken on the interaction loss L_int over the previous k steps D^(t,k). This happens in both training and testing, capped at 4 interaction-gradients per episode. Adapted θ_i is reset to θ for each episode.

Learned interaction loss L_int^φ: a 2-layer 1D temporal convolution (10×1 then 1×1 filters) over the concatenated past k LSTM hidden states and k policies. Its output's ℓ2 norm is the scalar loss. φ is frozen at test time and never updated by interaction-gradients.

Meta-training (outer loop): θ and φ are updated with Adam (β1=β2=1e-4) on L_nav evaluated with the adapted parameters θ_i over the full trajectory. This requires Hessian-vector products (MAML-style second-order). Training uses 12 asynchronous workers.

Hand-crafted alternatives: (1) a diversity loss that penalizes repeating the previous action in states judged the same by pixel-difference g; (2) a prediction loss, where BCE on a predicted action-success head q_θ is trained against a failure detected by frame similarity, and actions are sampled from π·q.

setting.backbone: ResNet18 (ImageNet-pretrained) features + GloVe target embedding + LSTM actor-critic, with a learned temporal-conv loss network (trained with A3C + meta-learning)
setting.training_data: AI2-THOR, 80 training scenes (20 each of kitchen/living room/bedroom/bathroom), with RL episodes using random target objects and start positions; 20 validation scenes for model selection

setting.action_space: discrete: MoveAhead, RotateLeft/RotateRight (45°), LookUp/LookDown (30° tilt), Done
setting.privileged: none for main method; 'GT obj' variant uses environment-provided termination signal

numbers_note: Table 1 reports means over 5 training runs with std. The failed-action ratio and the number-of-interaction-gradients ablation are shown only in figures, with no numbers in the text. The benchmark is the paper's own AI2-THOR (iTHOR, 120 single-room scenes) ObjectNav protocol, not RoboTHOR/ProcTHOR.
results: On unseen AI2-THOR scenes, SAVN reaches 40.86 SR / 16.15 SPL, versus 33.04 / 14.68 for the non-adaptive A3C baseline. It also beats Scene Priors (35.13 / 15.47) and a memory-augmented A3C (34.30 / 15.54). On episodes with optimal length ≥5 it gets 28.70 SR vs 21.44. With ground-truth termination it gets 54.40 SR vs 44.40 for A3C (GT obj). The learned loss beats both hand-crafted interaction losses, especially in SPL.
limitations: Second-order meta-gradients are costly, so at most 4 interaction-gradient steps are used per episode. Adaptation is reset every episode (no cross-episode accumulation).

Evaluated only in synthetic single-room AI2-THOR scenes with a coarse discrete action space. Absolute SPL remains low, and correct termination is a major failure source (GT-obj termination adds roughly 10–14 SR).
The hand-crafted variants rely on a pixel-similarity function g that the authors note may be unreliable in non-synthetic environments.
builds_on: Domain-adaptive meta-learning with learned loss (Yu et al. 2018, one-shot imitation from humans)
